recipe.title: Spinach, Tomato & Cottage Cheese Egg Muffins with Seeded Wholemeal Toast
recipe.description: Tender baked egg muffins with spinach, tomato and cottage cheese, seasoned with Dijon, smoked paprika and oregano, served with crisp seeded wholemeal toast for a practical high-protein weekday breakfast.

ingredients.notes: Whole eggs do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 150 g; retail carton size may vary.
Use 180 g; retail tub size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Use a thick cottage cheese so the muffin mixture does not become excessively wet.

ingredients.preparation: Wash if required and dry thoroughly.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 160 g; retail punnet size may vary.
Use 4 medium slices, 2 per serving. Check the package allergen declaration because seed blends vary.
ingredients.preparation: Keep sliced and ready for toasting.
ingredients.notes: Bread slice size and seed composition vary between products, so nutrition and allergens will vary slightly.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 1 tsp to grease the muffin tin.

ingredients.notes: Adds acidity and savoury depth to the egg mixture.
Cottage cheese and bread contribute additional salt.

equipment.notes: Used to bake the egg muffins.
Use a non-stick metal muffin tin if available.
Toast the bread while the egg muffins finish baking.

mise_en_place.instruction: Roughly chop the dry spinach into pieces approximately 15-20 mm across. Quarter the cherry tomatoes and place the pieces cut-side down briefly on clean kitchen paper or a clean towel to remove obvious surface juice.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The spinach is evenly chopped and the tomatoes are quartered without excess free liquid.

mise_en_place.instruction: Crack the 2 eggs into the mixing bowl. Add 150 g liquid egg whites, 180 g cottage cheese, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 tsp fine salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper.
mise_en_place.endpoint: All egg-muffin base ingredients are measured together and ready to mix.

procedure.title: Preheat and grease the muffin tin
procedure.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Use the 1 tsp olive oil to coat the base and lower sides of all 6 muffin holes in a thin, even film.
procedure.endpoint: The oven is fully preheated and the muffin tin has a continuous light oil coating with no large pools.

procedure.title: Mix the filling
procedure.instruction: Whisk the eggs, egg whites, cottage cheese and seasonings for approximately 30-45 seconds until the yolks are completely broken and the cottage cheese is evenly distributed but still visibly curded. Fold in the chopped spinach and quartered tomatoes.
procedure.endpoint: The mixture is evenly combined, with vegetables distributed throughout and no separate pools of egg white.

corrective_actions.condition: A large amount of tomato juice collects in the mixture.
corrective_actions.action: Spoon off the obvious free liquid before filling the muffin tin so the muffins bake rather than steam.

procedure.title: Fill and bake the egg muffins
procedure.instruction: Divide the egg mixture evenly between the 6 prepared muffin holes. Bake at 200°C for approximately 14-16 minutes.
procedure.endpoint: The muffins are puffed and lightly golden at the edges, the centres are fully set rather than liquid, and a gentle press on the centre springs back without releasing raw egg.

corrective_actions.condition: The tops brown strongly while the centres still appear wet.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the oven to 180°C and continue baking for 2-3 minutes until the centres are set.

corrective_actions.condition: The muffins remain pale and visibly soft after 16 minutes.
corrective_actions.action: Continue baking in 1-minute increments until the centres pass the stated set test.

procedure.title: Toast the seeded wholemeal bread
procedure.instruction: During the final few minutes of baking, toast the 4 slices of seeded wholemeal bread until the surfaces are crisp and golden while the centres remain tender.
procedure.endpoint: The bread is evenly toasted with crisp surfaces and no burnt seed or crust areas.

corrective_actions.condition: The exposed seeds begin darkening rapidly.
corrective_actions.action: Stop the toaster early rather than allowing the seed topping to burn.

procedure.title: Rest and release the muffins
procedure.instruction: Remove the muffin tin from the oven and leave the muffins to stand for approximately 2 minutes. Run a blunt knife or thin spatula around the edges only where necessary, then lift the muffins out carefully.
procedure.endpoint: The muffins release intact, remain tender and hold their shape without obvious liquid escaping.

corrective_actions.condition: A muffin sticks firmly to the tin.
corrective_actions.action: Leave it for another minute, then loosen the full circumference before attempting to lift it.

plating.instruction: Serve 3 warm spinach, tomato and cottage-cheese egg muffins per person with 2 slices of crisp seeded wholemeal toast. Eat immediately while the muffin centres remain tender and the toast is still crisp.

storage.storage_instructions: Cool leftover egg muffins promptly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Keep bread separate and toast it fresh when possible. Egg muffins may be frozen for up to 1 month once completely cool, with parchment between layers.
reheating_methods: Air fryer: reheat egg muffins at approximately 160°C for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout, checking early to avoid drying them.
Oven: reheat at approximately 170°C until piping hot throughout.
Toast fresh seeded wholemeal bread separately immediately before serving.

either_retailer: Liquid egg whites — 1 carton; use 150 g.
Low-fat cottage cheese — 1 tub; use 180 g.
Seeded wholemeal bread — 1 loaf; use 4 slices.

restaurant_quality_features: Cottage cheese keeps the egg muffins tender while adding substantial protein.
Dijon mustard provides acidity and savoury depth without requiring a separate sauce.
Smoked paprika and oregano give the vegetables and eggs a rounded aromatic profile.
Tomatoes are dried of obvious surface juice before baking so the muffins remain set rather than watery.
Seeded wholemeal toast provides a crisp contrast to the soft egg muffins.
Whole eggs provide richness while liquid egg whites raise protein efficiently without excessive calories.
nutrition_notes: Approximately 405 kcal and 37 g protein per serving.
Eggs, liquid egg whites and cottage cheese provide the majority of the protein.
Spinach and tomatoes add vegetable volume and micronutrients.
Seeded wholemeal toast supplies wholegrain carbohydrate, fibre and additional protein.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary with the exact cottage cheese, egg-white and bread products used.
critical_success_factors: Dry the spinach and tomatoes sufficiently before adding them to the egg mixture.
Grease all muffin holes thoroughly enough to allow clean release.
Do not over-whisk the cottage cheese into a completely smooth mixture; retaining small curds improves texture.
Bake until the centres are fully set but stop before the muffins become dry or rubbery.
Toast the bread during the final baking period so both components are ready together.
